subject: alebrije
pitch:
Category: Fantastical creature.
Subject: alebrije jaguar-eagle.
Style: Oaxacan alebrije painted wood.
reasoning:
I'm planning a compact but detailed alebrije design combining a jaguar body with an eagle head—hooked beak, folded or extended wings, feathered tail, and bright painted dots and swirls—aiming for a rest pose with separated legs, extended wings, and an articulated jaw, all within a manageable scope.

Now I'm working out the skeleton proportions: a jaguar roughly 1.2m long and 0.75m at the shoulder, with hip, spine, and neck joints positioned along a curved path, plus a tail chain extending backward with its own series of points. I'm structuring the spine and neck as parented joint chains feeding into the head, and planning to loft the body as a swept shape following the spine path with varying radii.

For the surface finish, I'm leaning toward a flat jaguar-yellow coat with painted spots for that alebrije look, keeping the paint technique simple and sparing rather than overly detailed.

Now I'm working out the body proportions, extending the spine path from hips to chest with rounded sweep caps to get the right overall length, then moving on to positioning the front legs from shoulder to foot.

For the limbs, I'm defining joint chains with lengths and bend directions—front legs with elbows bending back, hind legs with three-segment chains through hip, knee, and hock to foot, sizing the segment lengths so they sum to more than the vertical reach for a natural bent-leg look.

Each leg needs four named joints (hip/shoulder, knee/elbow, ankle/wrist, foot tip) since a chain of N points gives N-1 spans but needs N names to include the tip. I'm parenting hind legs to the root/hips and front legs to the spine tip, making sure joint names stay unique per side with suffixes, then sweeping tapered radii along each chain to build the leg geometry.

For feet, I'm giving the front legs jaguar-style paws and the hind legs eagle talons with feathered thighs, building each foot from a base part plus three forward toe capsules ending in claw spikes, sized and positioned so the paw ellipsoid sits just above the ground plane.

Continuing the neck chain toward the head with a tapering radius, then adding a feather ruff as a ring of outward-angled spikes around a neck joint, adjusting tilt so the feathers lean back along the neck direction rather than forward.

Now planning the head joint and skull shape, then sketching the eagle's hooked upper beak as a curved bone built from a few key points with a tapering radius, plus a shorter jawbone offset below and behind it to serve as the lower beak.

Still defining beak features... now I'm placing the eyes as yellow spheres with black pupils positioned outward and forward, adding angled eyebrow ridges, then designing the head crest as five fanning feather shapes extruded from a leaf outline.

Writing feather geometry helper...

Now I'm planning the wing bone chain attached at the shoulders, with joints for shoulder, elbow, and wrist sweeping outward from the spine, then rows of feathers distributed along that chain.

Working out primary feather placement and orientation, sweeping back from the wrist with increasing length toward the tip, colored across the alebrije palette, and figuring out the correct axes so each feather forms a flat horizontal blade rather than a vertical plane.

Now I'm adding tip-dot decorations and mid-line rods to each feather, layering shorter covert feathers slightly higher and forward, and wiring up bone/chain data so each feather call gets both position and bone from the wing chain points via the along helper.

For wing coverage, I'm planning 8 secondary feathers along the full chain plus 8 coverts, skipping a membrane. For the tail, I'm sketching a feathered fan at the tip—placing a ring of long eagle-style feathers at the tail's end point with manual positioning rather than relying on the ring helper, since the geometry there feels trickier to get right automatically.

Working out the feather fan math...

I'm mapping out the tail sweep path with four waypoints tapering back and down, alternating tube colors by segment, then adding small dorsal spikes along the spine using the body sweep for that alebrije-style decorative touch.

For the body texture I'm scattering around 70 small colored dot-sticks across the surface, excluding the underside, then layering 18 larger rosette markings with a dark outer ring and yellow inner dot—fixing a z-fighting issue by making the inner cylinder taller so it sits above the outer ring instead of sinking to the same depth.

Now I'm expanding the rosette palette to three layers (magenta outer, turquoise mid, yellow inner) via a reusable dot-stack helper, applying it more sparsely to legs and neck too. For the overall body coloring I'm setting a jaguar-gold base with a turquoise belly sector carved out by angle range.

I'm adding a magenta dorsal stripe sector, then thinking through leg coloring -- mostly gold with turquoise "sock" bands near the paws via a threshold color function along the sweep. I'm considering feathered details on the hind thighs, like small spike extrusions suggesting feathers, instead of a solid pant shape.

No eagle ears needed, but I'm adding small round jaguar-style ears with pink inner surfaces near the top of the head to give it a hybrid look, alongside dark brow ridges over the eyes for an eagle-like facial disc, and possibly a few scattered decorative dots on the skull surface for texture.

For the skeleton, I'm building a neck chain from the chest up to the head base using a catmull path with two named joints, parented to the spine tip. The spine itself runs from the hips forward to the chest as a three-point path, giving two spans plus a tip joint, with the hips joint anchored at the first point.

Then I'm sweeping the body along the spine chain as the source geometry, adjusting the chest radius so the front extends slightly past the chest point. I'm repositioning the head forward along the neck so the beak sits ahead of the chest front, and shrinking the wingspan down from 2.7 to about ±1.1 for proportion, before starting the wing chain.

I'm defining a radius function for the sweep varying chest-to-hip taper with a slight sinusoidal bulge, then using the resulting sweep as the surface source for scattering feathers, allowing hits that land on the sweep's end caps.

Now I'm working out the wing chain's four control points, moving from shoulder outward and back to form the wing curve, naming each joint segment and assigning the wing role, with the chain parented to the spine's upper joint near the chest. I'm handling left/right side naming with an L/R suffix, and setting up feather rows along the wing using an `along` distribution with a primary feather generator oriented backward based on position along the chain.

Still writing feather layout...

Rounding out the palette, I'm setting up the head and jaw joints parented to the neck chain, then writing a foot helper function and chain builders for the legs that take point arrays and roles.

For the limb chains I'm working out bend directions per joint—front elbow bending back, hind knee bending forward and hock back—so the sweep geometry curves naturally, then sweeping each chain with a radius function and sock coloring.

Naming the joint chains for each leg (hipHL, kneeHL, hockHL, footHL for hind; shoulderL through pawFL for front), then setting foot positions and talon shapes with longer curved claws for the hind feet, including a backward hallux. I'm also adding the eagle's thigh "pants" feathers hanging down near the hind hip, positioning them with a vertical extrusion and thickness along the side axis.

Now I'm placing those thigh feathers precisely relative to the hip joint and thigh sweep, then considering a chest bib detail—maybe a row of small colorful feather spikes, or just relying on the alebrije dot patterns plus a ring ruff around the chest. I'm starting to write the helper functions for placing dots and stacking shapes.

Writing feather helper function...

Now I'm working out the dorsal spike placement with an index counter, then defining head geometry—setting the skull center point and sphere scale for the head shape, followed by positioning the eyes along the skull's curved surface using the sphere equation to find the correct lateral offset.

Placing the pupil, highlight, and fierce angled brow (sloping down toward the beak like an eagle) using capsule shapes, plus a larger eye-ring sphere behind the eye for emphasis.

Now working out the beak geometry: defining the hooked upper beak path curving down to a point, the lower jaw bone shape, and the jaw joint pivot location that aims toward the jaw tip.

I'm setting up the neck ruff with two rings of alternating-colored spikes tilted around the neck at different points, then sketching out a five-feather crest fanning back from the top rear of the skull with directional vectors for each feather.

Now I'm working through the tail feather fan with its color gradient, confirming the rig names are solid, and checking that feet and talon claws rest correctly at floor level. I'm defining leg radius tapering functions for the hind and front legs, and setting up a scatter of body dots while skipping the legs.

I'm placing rosettes and neck dots with min-distance scatter functions, deciding the body color sectors (turquoise belly, magenta dorsal band), and accepting that small overlaps between rosettes and dots are fine visually.
